Kevin Trudeau asks a question that doesn't fit the usual story: why do some people with very low cholesterol get major blockages, while others with sky-high cholesterol keep arteries that stay wide open?

His answer: the amount of cholesterol in your blood isn't the deciding factor on its own.

Kevin's view: cholesterol itself isn't the villain. Your body needs both LDL and HDL. He says they're part of how your brain functions and how your hormones stay balanced.

The question he leaves you with: if cholesterol were simply bad, why would your body be built to run on it?
